stories.title: The New School Sells Loeb Hall Residence to Hawkins Way Capital for $52M
stories.excerpt: In its third acquisition of student housing in Manhattan this summer, Hawkins Way Capital has purchased a residence hall near Union Square for $51.5 million from the New School, according to city records made public Tuesday. Hawkins, using the entity 135 E 12th Owner, bought Loeb Hall, a 268-bed residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street, directly from The New School, records show. Joshua Bird, managing director and general counsel at Hawkins, signed the deal for the buyer, while Loretta Ferrari, chief financial officer at the New School, signed for the seller. “We’ve long been looking for the right opportunity in this neighborhood, and this property represents an ideal addition to our portfolio,” Ross Walker, managing partner at Hawkins, said in a statement to Commercial Observer. “Its location, existing student housing infrastructure and flexibility put us in an ideal position to deliver high-quality accommodations in one of the country’s strongest urban student housing markets.” It’s unclear why the New School stopped using Loeb Hall as an active dormitory for its students, but the property was removed from its undergraduate housing options this year. Loeb Hall is four blocks east of the New School’s main University Center and administrative offices on Fifth Avenue, although the sprawling urban campus has numerous sites near Union Square. The former Loeb Hall will undergo renovations and be repositioned under Hawkins’ Found Study student housing platform, according to a spokesperson for Hawkins. It’s unclear who brokered the recent sale. A spokesperson for the New School did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The deal is Hawkins’ third major student housing acquisition in Manhattan in recent months. In June, the Beverly Hills, Calif.-based firm acquired the Stratford Residence Hall at 117 West 70th Street on the Upper West Side from the American Musical and Dramatic Academy for $80 million, as CO previously
bullets: Hawkins Way Capital acquires 268-bed student housing at 131 E 12th St, Manhattan for $51.5M
Third student housing acquisition by Hawkins in Manhattan this summer signals operator confidence
New School divesting student housing; unclear rationale but signals institutional asset rotation
stories.summary: Hawkins Way Capital purchased Loeb Hall, a 268-bed residence hall near Union Square, from The New School for $51.5 million. This is Hawkins' third student housing acquisition in Manhattan within a single summer, indicating aggressive portfolio expansion in the submarket. The buyer highlighted the property's location, existing infrastructure, and flexibility as key value drivers in what it calls one of the country's strongest urban student housing markets.
stories.impact: Repeated institutional student housing acquisitions by a single operator in Manhattan signals strong cap-rate compression and capital availability for residential assets in tight submarkets; however, it also reflects universities offloading real estate, which may accelerate conversion of dorm capacity to market-rate housing and create supply-side headwinds for multifamily operators competing for young professional renters in Lower Manhattan/East Village.

stories.title: MetroStar Signs New Headquarters Lease at Reston Town Center
stories.excerpt: MetroStar Systems LLC, a Reston-based government IT contractor serving primarily defense and national security agencies, has signed a 37,844-square-foot lease at Reston Town Center.The new office, secured by JLL, will be located at 12010 Sunset Hills Road in Reston, Virginia, and represents the latest real estate move supporting MetroStar’s broader national growth plans and continued investment in expanding its capabilities and business following its acquisition by Veritas Capital in late 2025. JLL’s Jay Farmer and Steve Burman represented MetroStar in the transaction. BXP, the building owner, represented itself in the deal.MetroStar plans to relocate its Northern Virginia office to the new space in 2027 from its current location at 1856 Old Reston Avenue in Reston. The nine-story building is located in the heart of Reston Town Center, adjacent to the Reston Town Center Metro station, and features amenities including a fitness center. The post MetroStar Signs New Headquarters Lease at Reston Town Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MetroStar Systems leases 37,844 SF at Reston Town Center, Reston VA following Veritas Capital acquisition
Government IT contractor expanding office footprint post-acquisition; signals growth in defense/national security sector
Reston office market absorbing corporate tenant growth tied to Fed contractor consolidation
stories.summary: MetroStar Systems, a Reston-based government IT contractor, signed a 37,844-square-foot lease at Reston Town Center (12010 Sunset Hills Road) following its acquisition by Veritas Capital in late 2025. The transaction, brokered by JLL, represents MetroStar's strategic expansion to support national growth and expanded capabilities in defense and national security.
stories.impact: Government contractor growth and consolidation in Northern Virginia, driven by defense spending and PE backing, signals sustained employment growth in Reston and surrounding submarkets; this supports office utilization but also drives demand for corporate housing and nearshore multifamily for high-income federal IT workers, particularly in Reston/Herndon/Dulles corridor submarkets.

stories.title: Lee & Associates Lists Historic 80K-SF Ballard Building for Sale
stories.excerpt: Lee & Associates announced that the Ballard Building, a historic mixed-use asset, has been listed for sale. Lee & Associates is marketing the 99-year-old property at 2208 NW Market St. for an undisclosed price. The firm’s Scotty Rowe, Alex Muir, Stuart Williams and McCallum Mead are brokering the sale. The property features prominent street-level retail, professional office suites, and a penthouse apartment unit. At 98% occupancy, the Ballard Building represents an opportunity to acquire a generational legacy asset at a basis well below replacement. The six-story, 80,000-square-foot building has six ground-floor retail tenants, four floors of office space and a penthouse apartment. Ballard Health Club occupies the property’s lower level. The property features a diverse mix of established ground-floor retail, boutique professional office suites, and a penthouse apartment overlooking historic Ballard Avenue and the Lake Washington Ship Canal. CKM Associates LLP, a partnership owned by several local Ballard residents, purchased the building in 1983. The post Lee & Associates Lists Historic 80K-SF Ballard Building for Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 99-year-old Ballard Building (80,000 SF mixed-use) listed for sale at undisclosed price, 98% occupied
Six-story Seattle asset includes 6 retail tenants, 4 office floors, penthouse; held since 1983
Historic property marketed as 'generational legacy asset' below replacement cost
stories.summary: Lee & Associates is marketing the Ballard Building, a 99-year-old, 80,000-square-foot mixed-use property at 2208 NW Market St. in Seattle, for an undisclosed price. The six-story asset is 98% occupied with six ground-floor retail tenants, four floors of professional office, a penthouse apartment, and Ballard Health Club on the lower level. Owned by local partnership CKM Associates since 1983, it is positioned as a legacy acquisition opportunity below replacement cost.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development; asset is mixed-use office/retail/residential with minimal residential component (one penthouse unit). However, strong Ballard retail/entertainment district fundamentals evidenced by near-full occupancy and long-term local ownership suggest neighborhood demand; Seattle multifamily developers should note Ballard's continued resilience as a high-demand urban submarket worthy of nearby site assembly.

stories.title: Fifth Third, CB&T TruAmerica Lend $124M on Bay Area Apartments Build
stories.excerpt: SummerHill Apartment Communities (SHAC) has landed $123.5 million of construction financing to build a multifamily project in the San Francisco Bay Area, Commercial Observer has learned. Fifth Third Bank and California Bank & Trust (CB&T) provided a $96.5 million senior construction loan for the developer’s planned apartment community in San Carlos, Calif. TruAmerica Multifamily also closed a $27 million preferred equity investment to support the six-story San Mateo County development, which is slated to commence construction soon. The deal marked TruAmerica Multifamily’s first preferred equity financing since launching a structured finance platform last year. The new business vertical was formed following the addition of Ash Baraghoush, head of TruAmerica’s structured finance group, after he spent nearly a decade at Pacific Urban Investors. “This really goes hand in hand with the firm’s transformation into being a residential investment management company and being able to speak throughout the entire capital stack as opposed to just being owner operators,” Baraghoush told Commercial Observer. “We have spent a good year-plus cultivating new relationships.” Located at 11 El Camino Real 24 miles south of Downtown San Francisco, the project will feature 251 apartments with 38 of the units designated as affordable housing. Baraghoush said San Carlos has plenty of tailwinds as a multifamily market given its close ties to the San Francisco Bay Area’s technology and life science industries. He noted that the San Carlos submarket has a 97 percent multifamily occupancy rate and the region has experienced double-digit rent growth. “The Bay Area as a market has certainly outperformed and is perhaps one of the one of the better performing markets in the nation right now driven by return to office and driven by the AI boom,” Baraghoush said. “The need for affordable workforce housing continues to remain and that’s one of the attractive natures for this
bullets: SummerHill Apartment Communities secures $123.5M construction financing for San Carlos, CA six-story project
Fifth Third Bank & CB&T provide $96.5M senior; TruAmerica adds $27M preferred equity
First preferred equity deal from TruAmerica's new structured finance platform; construction starts soon
stories.summary: SummerHill Apartment Communities landed $123.5 million in construction financing for a six-story multifamily development in San Carlos, California (San Mateo County). Fifth Third Bank and California Bank & Trust provided a $96.5 million senior construction loan, while TruAmerica Multifamily closed a $27 million preferred equity investment. This marks TruAmerica's first deal from its newly launched structured finance platform and signals active capital availability for Bay Area residential development.
stories.impact: Bay Area multifamily construction financing remains accessible and layered despite macro rate environment; emergence of structured equity platforms (TruAmerica) alongside traditional bank debt suggests capital stack flexibility for new supply in expensive coastal markets like San Francisco Bay Area, supporting continued deliveries and upward pricing pressure on rents in San Mateo County and surrounding submarkets.

stories.title: Sports Tech Firm Genius Sports Moves U.S. HQ to Vornado’s 1290 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Sports analytics and technology company Genius Sports is relocating its U.S. headquarters to 1290 Avenue of the Americas. The London-based company’s new 10-year lease with landlord Vornado Realty Trust spans 53,000 square feet across part of the tower’s sixth floor. Asking rent was $99 per square foot, according to The Real Deal, which first reported on the lease. Newmark’s Josh Berg and A.J. Dorn negotiated the deal on behalf of Genius Sports, while Vornado was represented in-house by Ryan Levy and Edward Riguardi. A spokesperson for the landlord declined to comment on the transaction. The deal offers Genius Sports a marked expansion from its 28,000-square-foot West Chelsea offices at 512 West 22nd Street. That building changed hands last year from Vornado and the Albanese Organization to Raghsa Real Estate for $205 million. Genius Sports’ arrival brings 1290 Avenue of the Americas to 95 percent occupancy. The 43-story, full-block building between 51st and 52nd streets is anchored by investment management firm Neuberger Berman, and recently underwent a $45 million renovation that updated lobby and building amenities. Vornado owns 70 percent of the building, while the Trump Organization holds a passive 30 percent stake. Other recent arrivals at the tower include business consulting firms Portage Point Partners and Protiviti, which CO reported leased a total of 93,000 square feet late last year. In January, investment manager Oaktree leased the building’s entire 12th floor, just a few stories below law firm Selendy Gay’s 101,000-square-foot offices. Spokespeople for Genius Sports and Newmark did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Genius Sports relocates US HQ from Chelsea to 1290 Avenue of Americas, 53,000 SF, 10-year lease
London-based sports tech firm expands from 28,000 SF West Chelsea office; asking rent $99/SF
Lease brings 1290 Ave of Americas to 95% occupancy; signals Midtown Plaza District office demand
stories.summary: Genius Sports, a London-based sports analytics and technology company, is relocating its U.S. headquarters to 1290 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown Manhattan under a 10-year lease spanning 53,000 square feet on the sixth floor. The move represents significant expansion from its current 28,000-square-foot West Chelsea office at 512 West 22nd Street. Asking rent was $99 per square foot; the lease brings the 43-story building to 95% occupancy.
stories.impact: Tech tenant upsizing and footprint consolidation in Midtown—rather than outbound migration—signals stabilization of Manhattan's office market for knowledge-work sectors; however, Genius Sports' departure from Chelsea/West 22nd Street underscores continued office flight from WeHo and downtown areas, which may depress nearby residential demand in those submarkets while Midtown and Plaza District continue absorbing corporate relocations and driving professional housing demand in adjacent neighborhoods.

stories.title: Data Center Developer Increases Land Holdings at Briscoe County Site
stories.excerpt: Soluna Holdings, a developer of green data centers for intensive computing applications, including AI and Bitcoin mining, closed the purchase of 397 acres in Briscoe County, Texas. The land will host Project Dorothy 3, Soluna’s planned renewable-first AI computing campus with a potential capacity of up to 300 MW. Briscoe County is between Amarillo and Lubbock. The parcel sits adjacent to Projects Dorothy 1 and 2 and to the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm, which Soluna acquired in April. The Briscoe Wind Farm’s Substation sits directly across from the acquired property, positioning Dorothy 3 for direct, behind-the-meter access to generation the Company owns outright.  The 397 acres exceed the 300 acres Soluna originally identified for the campus. The additional land gives the Company room to add data halls should further generation or storage capacity become available at the site.  Project Dorothy 3 is part of Soluna’s development pipeline of approximately 6.3 GW across multiple sites. Soluna currently operates approximately 192 MW of energized capacity.  The post Data Center Developer Increases Land Holdings at Briscoe County Site appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Soluna Holdings acquires 397 acres in Briscoe County, TX for Project Dorothy 3 AI data center campus
300 MW potential capacity; adjacent to owned 150 MW wind farm and existing Dorothy 1 & 2 projects
Land exceeds original 300-acre plan; additional acreage enables future data hall expansion
stories.summary: Soluna Holdings closed the purchase of 397 acres in Briscoe County, Texas (between Amarillo and Lubbock) for Project Dorothy 3, a planned renewable-first AI computing campus with up to 300 MW capacity. The parcel sits adjacent to Soluna's Projects Dorothy 1 and 2 and the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm acquired in April. The additional 97 acres above original plans provide expansion optionality for future data halls if generation capacity increases.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; however, large data center clusters in remote rural Texas may trigger downstream housing demand for technical workers and construction labor during phased buildout; Amarillo and Lubbock submarkets should monitor for indirect employment and population inflow, though scale of on-site permanent jobs likely remains modest relative to construction phase intensity—unlikely to materially drive apartment demand in these secondary markets.

stories.title: SJC Ventures Sells Whole Foods-Anchored Center in South Florida for $83M
stories.excerpt: SJC Ventures has sold a newly completed Whole Foods-anchored retail center in Doral, Fla., for $83 million, property records show. Called Doral Marketplace, the property spans 89,000 square feet at 10800 Northwest 41st Street, about a mile east of the Florida Turnpike and 14 miles west of Downtown Miami. Atlanta-based SJC Ventures completed the 10-acre strip mall last quarter. The sale excluded a 1.8-acre portion of the property leased to Chick-fil-A. Records list the buyer as Traditions Management, a Dallas-based developer and operator of senior living communities. The buyer assumed a loan with $50 million in outstanding debt, which has now been assigned to the Bank of Texas. Whole Foods is Doral Marketplace’s biggest tenant with a 43,000-square-foot location. Other tentants include J. Crew Factory, Ulta Beauty, Shake Shack, First Watch, GoodVets, The Spot Barbershop, Encore Nails, VIO MedSpa and Apizza Brooklyn Resto + Vino. The sale comes as Miami-Dade County retail leasing remains strong. During the second quarter of 2026, average asking rents jumped to $42.50 per square foot, up 2.6 percent quarter-over-quarter, while the vacancy rate fell to 3 percent. More than 1.3 million square feet of retail space remains under construction, including another Whole Foods location in South Beach, for which developer Russell Galbut nabbed a $54 million construction loan last year. Representatives for SJC Ventures and Traditions Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: SJC Ventures sells Whole Foods-anchored Doral Marketplace (89,000 SF) for $83M to Traditions Management
Buyer is Dallas-based senior living operator; assumes $50M loan; sale excludes 1.8-acre Chick-fil-A parcel
Miami-Dade Q2 2026 retail asking rents jumped 2.6% to $42.50/SF; strong leasing environment
stories.summary: SJC Ventures sold Doral Marketplace, a newly completed 89,000-square-foot Whole Foods-anchored strip mall in Doral, Florida, for $83 million to Traditions Management, a Dallas-based senior living developer. The buyer assumed a $50 million loan transferred to Bank of Texas. The sale excluded a 1.8-acre Chick-fil-A parcel. Whole Foods occupies 43,000 square feet; additional tenants include J. Crew Factory, Ulta Beauty, Shake Shack, and others. Miami-Dade retail asking rents rose 2.6% to $42.50/SF in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; primarily a retail/senior housing transaction. However, strong retail leasing fundamentals in Doral (2.6% YoY rent growth, 89,000 SF new supply absorbed) and conversion of retail-anchored real estate to senior living by PE-backed operators signals competitive pressure for land and capital in fast-growing West Dade submarkets—multifamily developers competing for infill or land-banking opportunities in Doral/Westchester corridor should expect elevated acquisition costs and rising competition from mixed-use/alternative-use buyers.

stories.title: KeyBank Expands to 113K SF at Elecor’s 1301 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: A major banking institution has added 15,292 square feet to its Manhattan office footprint, Commercial Observer has learned. Keybank signed a 15-year deal to renew its existing space and expand to 112,924 square feet at Elecor Properties’ 1301 Avenue of the Americas across the entire 35th, 36th and 37th floors, as well as portions of the 28th and 38th floors, according to the landlord. Asking rent for the Plaza District office tower was not disclosed, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown in the second quarter of 2026 was $86.18 per square foot, according to a report from CBRE. “As KeyBank continues to grow and adapt to the evolving needs of our business, we remain focused on providing our employees with an environment that fosters collaboration and connection,” John Manginelli, Hudson Valley and metro New York market president at KeyBank, said in a statement. “Expanding our footprint at 1301 Avenue of the Americas enables us to support that vision while positioning us for continued growth and enhanced service to our clients across the region.” JLL’s Matthew Astrachan, Justin Haber, Kyle Riker, Adam Hill and Bob Beckstedt represented KeyBank in the transaction, while Peter Brindley, Douglas Neye and Sean Kirk handled negotiations in-house for Elecor Properties. “This was a highly strategic transaction that addressed several priorities at once: securing more space for KeyBank’s growing businesses, keeping its teams together within one elevator bank, creating the opportunity to upgrade the existing workplace, and establishing a true New York City headquarters with prominent signage,” Astrachan said in a statement. Neye, Elecor’s senior vice president of leasing, added in a statement that the lease demonstrates the “enduring appeal of a high-quality, well-located workplace.” Other tenants in the building between West 52nd and West 53rd streets include investment bank Piper Sandler, which signed a lease for 140
bullets: KeyBank expands to 112,924 SF at 1301 Avenue of Americas, Manhattan; 15-year renewal + expansion deal
Occupies entire 35th, 36th, 37th floors plus portions of 28th & 38th; adds 15,292 SF to existing footprint
Midtown Plaza District average asking rent Q2 2026: $86.18/SF; major bank anchor signaling confidence
stories.summary: KeyBank signed a 15-year lease to renew and expand its Manhattan office footprint to 112,924 square feet at Elecor Properties' 1301 Avenue of the Americas, occupying the entire 35th, 36th, and 37th floors plus portions of the 28th and 38th floors. The expansion adds 15,292 square feet to the bank's existing space. Mid-town Plaza District average asking rent in Q2 2026 was $86.18 per square foot.
stories.impact: Major financial services tenant expansion in Midtown signals sustained demand for prime office space in Plaza District and confidence in NYC's financial hub despite hybrid work trends; however, expansion reflects consolidation and optimization of existing footprint (renewal + modest growth) rather than net new hiring, suggesting stable but not accelerating office employment; nearby multifamily (Midtown South, Plaza District) benefits from stable professional-class renters but should not assume significant inbound migration from this transaction alone.

stories.title: League City Developer Pursuing Nearly 300K-SF of Retail, Industrial Space
stories.excerpt: Alexander Grene Development broke ground on the $78 million mixed-use business park Lilac Field in League City. The development is seeking its first industrial and retail tenants. Located between League City Parkway and SH 146, Lilac Field will span 24.5 acres and include 70,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space and 220,000 square feet of flexible warehouse space. Community Impact reports once complete, Lilac Field will include 16 small warehouse units and seven retail and restaurant buildings, with warehouse tenants expected to include entertainment venues, gyms, childcare providers and breweries. The development’s first two industrial buildings are expected to be completed by early 2027. The developer is seeking industrial clients, such as aerospace and aviation suppliers, marine service groups, technology firms, energy service companies, advanced manufacturing users and specialty distributors to rent its warehouse space. The full buildout is projected to take three to five years. The post League City Developer Pursuing Nearly 300K-SF of Retail, Industrial Space appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Alexander Grene Development breaks ground on $78M Lilac Field mixed-use park, League City, TX
24.5 acres: 70,000 SF retail/restaurant + 220,000 SF warehouse (16 small units); Phase 1 complete early 2027
Targeting aerospace, marine, tech, advanced manufacturing tenants; first two industrial buildings begin 2027
stories.summary: Alexander Grene Development broke ground on Lilac Field, a $78 million mixed-use business park on 24.5 acres in League City, Texas (between League City Parkway and SH 146). The development will include 70,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space, 220,000 square feet of flexible warehouse space, 16 small warehouse units, and seven retail/restaurant buildings. First two industrial buildings are expected to complete by early 2027. The developer is recruiting aerospace, aviation, marine, tech, and advanced manufacturing tenants.
stories.impact: Flex/industrial and retail development in high-growth Houston suburb (League City is northeast Houston growth corridor) signals sustained demand for logistics and light manufacturing space; proximity of new industrial supply may siphon warehouse tenants from adjacent multifamily markets, but League City's population growth (driven by energy sector, petrochemical manufacturing, and Houston metro expansion) supports downstream residential demand—multifamily developers should target League City/Pasadena/Pearland corridor for workforce housing catering to industrial and energy sector employees.

stories.title: Prosper Developer Planning $240M Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: Developer Naseem Shaik is moving forward on a $240 million Prosper project that will include a hotel, offices, retail and restaurants. No multifamily is planned at the time. Dubbed Bella Prosper, it will sit on 61 acres with a large manmade lake in the middle. The development will incorporate one-story offices as well as office space above restaurant and retail spaces. Features of Bella Prosper include a 139-key hotel geared toward business travelers, a public parking deck and a park with a water feature. Bella Prosper is slated to build at least 60,950 square feet of retail space. Community Impact reports Bella Prosper is expected to create $59.8 million in annual taxable sales. Developers estimate that Bella Prosper as a whole will generate $88.3 million in net benefits for the town over the next 25 years. Construction on Phase 1 was originally expected to start in late 2027. The post Prosper Developer Planning $240M Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Developer Naseem Shaik planning $240M Bella Prosper mixed-use project on 61 acres, Prosper TX
139-key hotel, office, retail, restaurants; 60,950 SF retail planned; NO multifamily component announced
Phase 1 construction originally expected late 2027; projected $88.3M net benefit to Prosper over 25 years
stories.summary: Developer Naseem Shaik is advancing Bella Prosper, a $240 million mixed-use development on 61 acres in Prosper, Texas, featuring a 139-key hotel, office space, restaurants, retail, and a public parking deck. At least 60,950 square feet of retail is planned. Notably, no multifamily component is included. Phase 1 construction was originally expected to start in late 2027, with projections of $88.3 million in net benefits to the town over 25 years.
stories.impact: Mixed-use development in high-growth Dallas suburb (Prosper is north Dallas corridor) without residential component signals developer focus on hospitality, office, and retail; however, strong municipal economic impact projections and hotel development suggest sustained population/employment inflow—absence of multifamily in a $240M mixed-use project may indicate land constraints, zoning restrictions, or developer underweighting of housing demand, representing potential gap for competing multifamily operators to target nearby Prosper/Frisco submarkets with purpose-built apartment communities catering to hotel/office workers and regional commuters.
